name: USS New York
shortDescription: Slow, thick-skinned early battleship that hits hard and shrugs off punishment.

consumables.name: Damage Control Party
consumables.flavor: 20s action, 80s cooldown. A fire and a flood landing together will outlast it.

consumables.name: Repair Party
consumables.flavor: 3 charges, 28s each at 245 hp/s, about 6,860 hp per activation, close to a fifth of her max health pool.

turrets.note: Needs a full broadside to bring this turret to bear, the narrowest arc on the ship.

strengths: Heavy belt armor for the tier, bounces a lot of incoming AP
Ten guns hit hard even at range
Tanky enough to hold a flank alone if it has to
weaknesses: Painfully slow, easy to outmaneuver and hard to reposition
Sluggish turret traverse struggles to answer flanking attacks
Turret 3 needs a full broadside to fire at all, a third of her main battery is unavailable bow-on
Very exposed to torpedoes if caught out of position
tips: Pick your spot early and commit. You don't have the speed to change your mind halfway through.
Angle your bow toward incoming fire. That belt armor does its best work when you're not broadside.
Listen for torpedoes. You will not be dodging them with this turning circle.

threats.reason: Their torpedoes punish your lack of speed and maneuverability badly.
They can dictate range and kite you all game if you let them.

summary: Slow and heavily armored, built to plant on a flank and stay there.
Ten guns hit hard at range, more firepower than mobility.
Turning circle and top speed make her helpless against a flanking attack.
playstyle.detail: New York isn't going anywhere fast, and she doesn't need to. Plant her on a flank, angle that belt toward the enemy, and grind down anything that strays into range of her guns. The catch is commitment. Once you've picked a spot, you're mostly stuck defending it, so choose with care.

goalTags.note: Heavy armor and a broadside that punishes anyone careless enough to get close.
